what_this_is: a decomposition of the 12-point linear residual into its two components, plus the later correction that removed the mechanism originally proposed for the second one

data.grid: 12 k points, 0.02 to 3.0 h/Mpc, z=0, CAMB reference at 4096 points

component_1_smooth_tilt.value: about +1.25..1.50% below k=0.05, easing to +0.57..0.85% above k=0.25
component_1_smooth_tilt.note: a broadband offset, not an oscillation; it is the part the +0.74% median describes, and it is roughly the size of the whole 0.5% budget

component_2_bao_oscillation.implied_amplitude_excess: if our wiggle is A(1+delta) against CAMB's A, peak/trough = (1+delta)/(1-delta); 1.0275 gives delta = 1.36%, 1.0284 gives delta = 1.40%
component_2_bao_oscillation.so: our BAO wiggle is about 1.4% too strong, and the excess GROWS slightly with k (1.36% -> 1.40% across the two pairs)
component_2_bao_oscillation.mechanism: UNKNOWN - the Silk damping explanation originally proposed here was tested and refuted, see below

phase_is_not_implicated: the peak POSITION was separately shown to match to 5 decimals (ln k = -4.0824 on both sides, shift = 0.00000, ratio 1.0088 at the peak top), so this is an amplitude defect and not a phase defect. A phase error would put the residual 90 degrees out of phase with the wiggle; the measured residual is in phase with it.

RETRACTED_silk_damping_explanation.what_was_claimed_here_first: that an amplitude excess growing with k is the signature of Silk damping being slightly too weak, and that damping would need to be 1-2% stronger
RETRACTED_silk_damping_explanation.why_it_was_plausible: damping suppresses more at higher k, so a weaker damping leaves progressively more wiggle at high k, which is the observed shape
RETRACTED_silk_damping_explanation.how_it_was_tested: scaled kappa by S in PerturbationBatch.coefficients, with tc_epsilon scaled by 1/S so the tight-coupling switch fires at the same time and only the damping changes. Measured P(0.17)/P_CAMB at S = 2.00, 1.20, 1.00, 0.80, 0.50.
RETRACTED_silk_damping_explanation.sensitivity: -1.93% per unit ln kappa around S=1
RETRACTED_silk_damping_explanation.why_that_refutes_it: removing the 2.49% excess would need ln kappa up by 1.29, i.e. opacity multiplied by 3.6. That is not a correction to a recombination history; it would wreck the damping tail, and the high-k ratios sit at only +0.57..0.77%.
RETRACTED_silk_damping_explanation.consistency_check_that_validates_the_mea: the earlier +-2% kappa experiment reported 0.039pp; ln(1.02)*1.93% = 0.038pp. The measurement was right all along - it was the inference from it that was wrong.

what_that_leaves: two measured defects, both about the size of the whole error budget, and NEITHER has a known mechanism. The residual is now a description rather than an explanation.
hypotheses_from_the_acoustic_sector_that: CAMB's second-order tight-coupling EXIT values - broke k=0.05 outright, dropped
CAMB's tight-coupling epsilon (0.0325/0.02 against our 0.1) - low k worse, high k diverged to 1.7e210
baryon lag - agrees with CAMB to 4e-4, not the cause
baryon sound speed - a 10x change moves dm in the 8th digit
Silk damping - refuted above, sensitivity two orders of magnitude too small

status_against_target.verdict: not met, 5x over at the BAO peak
